claims.text: A controlled solidification process using a two-stage cooling protocol can produce a bimodal grain-size distribution in eutectic high-entropy alloys.
The targeted bimodal microstructure contains fine grains of approximately 100 nm and coarse grains of approximately 10 μm.
Introducing this bimodal grain-size distribution will create a hierarchical microstructure.
The fine-grained population increases strength through grain-boundary strengthening.
The coarse-grained population increases ductility through strain hardening.
Grain-boundary interactions contribute to the increased ductility of the bimodal microstructure.
Alloying elements may contribute to the proposed strength–ductility improvement.
Combining fine and coarse grains will simultaneously increase strength and ductility relative to a uniform grain-size baseline.
The intervention is expected to increase yield strength by 20% relative to the uniform-grain-size baseline.
The intervention is expected to increase elongation to failure by 30% relative to the uniform-grain-size baseline.
The quantified predicted improvements are based on simulations and prior experimental results.
The proposed improvement should hold at operating temperatures below 500°C and applied stresses from 100 MPa to 500 MPa.
Above 500°C, significant microstructural changes or degradation may occur.
The magnitude of the improvement may depend on alloy composition, processing conditions, and operating environment.
